proposed_edges.relationship: In “Interview: Steven Shapin” (2025; recorded July 2024), Shapin recalls that reading Rosenberg’s papers on American agricultural research led him to apply to Pennsylvania’s history-of-science programme in the hope of working with Rosenberg.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Fresh primary retrospective testimony: publisher PDF, printed p. 3, paragraph beginning “Only one of my applications”, within the first autobiographical answer (pp. 2–5). Shapin says his reason for applying was reading Rosenberg’s agricultural-history papers; his hope of thesis supervision “didn’t work out that way”. He identifies subsequent friendship and departmental colleagueship. This supports a specific reading-mediated career influence, not doctoral supervision or adoption of Rosenberg’s entire method. The individual papers are not identified here and were not read; their publication years are not inferred. Interview date is on p. 1; original publication was June 2025.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Carroll Smith-Rosenberg, Rosenberg’s “The Female Animal” (1973) examines how nineteenth-century medical and biological arguments defended traditional sex roles against women’s demands for education and reproductive choice.
proposed_edges.map_label: Medical arguments and traditional sex roles, 1973
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Read the licensed preview of the 1987 anthology From ‘Fair Sex’ to Feminism, chapter opening pp. 13–15 (PDF pages 28–30): https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781135175702_A23800116/preview-9781135175702_A23800116.pdf. p. 13 identifies an analysis of “normative descriptions of the female role”; p. 14 specifies education, birth control and abortion, and medicine’s legitimation of inherited roles. Both coauthors are credited. Publisher metadata and anthology acknowledgements establish original publication in September 1973, not 1987 or the preview’s 2004 reprint. The original journal scan and remaining essay were not read. This is a bounded contribution concerning gender roles, not a claim to found gender history or anticipate its later theoretical positions.

review.reviewer: Claude (independent verification agent; coordinator decisions by Claude)
review.phrase_seen: employed medical and biological arguments to rationalize traditional sex roles
review.reason: Licensed publisher preview, anthology pp. 13-14 (text layer present): 'normative descriptions of the female role'; the essay 'examines the ideological attack ... against ... women's demands for improved educational opportunities and their decision to resort to birth control and abortion'. Both coauthors credited. Anthology acknowledgements say it 'appeared in the Journal in September 1973'. Sentence supported. Endpoint note: the essay is framed as women's role / sex roles in 1973; `women` (Women's history) would be an equally or more natural target than `gender` (Gender history); reviewer's call. No duplicate edge.
